angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 158,341 km at 73.08 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.6842 +/- 0.0532 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 73.08 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2276 +/- 0.0057 solar radii from Bryant et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6894 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025NatAs...9.1031B/abstract): 158,341 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.207 +/- 0.011 solar masses from Bryant et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6894 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025NatAs...9.1031B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3007 +/- 58 K from Bryant et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6894 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025NatAs...9.1031B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bryant et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6894 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025NatAs...9.1031B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6894.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.040, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
